title: Protocol for assembling micro- and nanoparticles in a viscous liquid above a vibrating plate
author: Shabaniverki, Thorud, et al.

steps.title: Gather materials and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect glass microparticles (425–600 µm, Sigma‑Aldrich G8772), iron (II, III) oxide nanoparticles (50–100 nm, Alfa Aesar 47,141), DI water (ARIES system, 0.2 µm filter), epoxy, a screw, a 95‑mm diameter polystyrene petri dish (Fisher FB0875714G), a function generator (Vizatek 01VZMFG2120), a mechanical wave driver (Pasco SF‑9324), and a Canon PowerShot SX530 HS camera (16 MP).

steps.title: Prepare vibrating petri dish
steps.instruction: Attach a centered screw to the bottom of the 95‑mm polystyrene petri dish using epoxy; allow the epoxy to cure for 24 h, then mount the dish onto the moving arm of the mechanical wave driver that will receive the sinusoidal waveform from the function generator.

steps.title: Prepare particle dispersions
steps.instruction: Add 20 mL of filtered DI water to the mounted petri dish. For microparticle experiments, add 1.5 g of the glass beads to the water; for nanoparticle experiments, add 1 g of iron oxide nanoparticles to the water. Gently mix to obtain a uniform dispersion.

steps.title: Connect generator and set up imaging
steps.instruction: Connect the function generator to the mechanical wave driver with a banana connector. Position a tripod with the Canon PowerShot SX530 HS camera directly above the petri dish to capture images of the particle patterns.

steps.title: Set vibration parameters and run experiment
steps.instruction: Program the function generator to output sinusoidal voltages with amplitudes ranging from 2 V to 6 V and frequencies from 100 Hz to 2000 Hz. Activate the wave driver to vibrate the petri dish. Observe particle migration: glass microparticles migrate to displacement anti‑nodes and form clusters within 40–50 s after start; nanoparticles respond according to size‑dependent mechanisms.

substeps.instruction: Select a voltage amplitude (e.g., 2 V, then increase up to 6 V).
Select a frequency (e.g., start at 100 Hz, then step through to 2000 Hz).
Start the vibration and allow 40–50 s for pattern formation before changing parameters.

steps.title: Capture and record patterns
steps.instruction: Using the camera, photograph the particle arrangements at each frequency and voltage setting to document the assembled micro‑ and nanoparticle structures.
